profiles.name: egress
profiles.preparation: closed-loop (each request waits for its response before the next is sent; no scheduled arrival) over the frame protocol, plaintext workload dialler to a mesh peer on loopback; 10 warm-up then 100 sequential connections (connect, first byte, handshake), then one connection of 200 warm-up and 10000 timed 64-byte round trips (tail latency) and one connection carrying one 256 MiB frame (throughput). Baseline arm plaintext-baseline: the same dialler, bound the same way, connects straight to a plaintext TCP peer with no intercept worker, no nft rules and no TLS. Arm composed-mtls: the dialler's flow is registered with the real intercept worker and captured on leg F, which runs mTLS over kTLS to a rustls mesh peer that requires a client certificate; peer tickets disabled; handshake is the enforce duration; resource rows are whole-host scope (the aggregate cpu line of /proc/stat over every CPU and every process, no cgroup figure; each ratio is the class's tick delta over the delta of all CPU time, idle included) sampled across the 256 MiB throughput window, with memory (VmRSS) and open sockets of the benchmark process taken at its end; forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are the mtls-out-fwd and mtls-out-ret threads' share of the CPU the process's threads outside the family's own ovbm- threads accrued in that window, and because the window carries the request one way the return pump is the light one; thread CPU is read in 10 ms ticks, so the heavy-to-light ratio (record note pump_heavy_to_light_lower_bound) is a lower bound

profiles.name: ingress
profiles.preparation: closed-loop (each request waits for its response before the next is sent; no scheduled arrival) over the frame protocol, client to the node's inbound path on loopback with an in-memory guest end; 10 warm-up then 100 sequential connections (connect, first byte, handshake), then one connection of 200 warm-up and 10000 timed 64-byte round trips (tail latency) and one connection carrying one 256 MiB frame (throughput). Baseline arm plaintext-baseline: a plaintext client to a loopback listener that bridges each connection to the same in-memory guest sink, with no TLS and no enforcement. Arm composed-mtls: a rustls client presenting a node-trusted certificate to the real HostMtlsEnforcement serving Routed::Inbound over loopback leg C; the guest transport is excluded, and first byte includes the client side of the TLS handshake; resource rows are whole-host scope (the aggregate cpu line of /proc/stat over every CPU and every process, no cgroup figure; each ratio is the class's tick delta over the delta of all CPU time, idle included) sampled across the 256 MiB throughput window, with memory (VmRSS) and open sockets of the benchmark process taken at its end; forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are absent because the relay is asynchronous on shared runtime threads

notes.cpu_scope: whole host: the aggregate cpu line of /proc/stat over every CPU and every process (interrupt and kernel-worker time is charged outside any benchmark cgroup); each host_cpu_*_ratio is the class's tick delta over the delta of all CPU time, idle included, across the throughput window; user includes nice
notes.ingress_handshake_scope: handshake_ns on ingress starts when the enforcement accepts the connection, so it includes the wait for the client's ClientHello (client-side TLS work)
notes.pump_cpu_resolution: per-thread CPU is read from /proc/self/task/*/stat in 10 ms ticks, so the lighter pump can read below one tick and the heavy-to-light ratio (pump_heavy_to_light_lower_bound) is a lower bound
notes.pump_cpu_scope: egress composed-mtls: forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are the mtls-out-fwd and mtls-out-ret threads' share of the CPU the process's threads accrued over the throughput window, leaving out the family's own threads (fixture_thread_prefix); the window carries the 256 MiB request one way, so the return pump is the light one
notes.resource_scope: memory_bytes is this process's VmRSS and socket_count its open socket descriptors, both sampled at the end of the throughput window with its connection still open; connection_concurrency is the connections the client holds open in that window
notes.tls_peer_colocated: the TLS peer (egress) or TLS client (ingress) runs on the same host as the agent and may co-limit throughput and tail latency; the numbers are not pure agent cost

notes.ingress_handshake_scope: handshake_ns on ingress starts when the enforcement accepts the connection, so it includes the wait for the client's ClientHello (client-side TLS work)
notes.pump_cpu_resolution: per-thread CPU is read from /proc/self/task/*/stat in 10 ms ticks, so the lighter pump can read below one tick and the heavy-to-light ratio (pump_heavy_to_light_lower_bound) is a lower bound
notes.pump_cpu_scope: egress composed-mtls: forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are the mtls-out-fwd and mtls-out-ret threads' share of the CPU the process's threads accrued over the throughput window, leaving out the family's own threads (fixture_thread_prefix); the window carries the 256 MiB request one way, so the return pump is the light one
notes.resource_scope: memory_bytes is this process's VmRSS and socket_count its open socket descriptors, both sampled at the end of the throughput window with its connection still open; connection_concurrency is the connections the client holds open in that window
notes.tls_peer_colocated: the TLS peer (egress) or TLS client (ingress) runs on the same host as the agent and may co-limit throughput and tail latency; the numbers are not pure agent cost
